title: When the Passage Wakes
premise: Coral Zhou, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy forbids anyone to name, is pulled from the water by a dying prospector who trades him a hand-drawn map of the Kestrel Range for one promise: deliver it to a woman named Ada Voss before the first snows seal the passes. The map marks something the navy sank deliberately — and both the service that buried it and the syndicate that paid for its silence will kill to keep it lost. Crossing the range with a found family of outcasts he never asked for, Coral must choose between loyalty to the people who saved him and the truth the map carries. In the end he opens the pass at the cost of his salvage claim, exposes the sinking through Ada's testimony, and walks away with no fortune but the family that chose to follow him.
about_author: Emrys Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent six seasons charting cold-water wrecks before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people the wilderness keeps honest.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Coral Zhou dives a navy-cordoned wreck in grey water, salvaging what the sea allows, POV Coral. He finds a hull plate stamped with a serial number that shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: restless competence shadowed by the sense that the water is keeping secrets from him.

chapters.title: A Map for a Promise
chapters.summary: Still POV Coral. A half-drowned prospector, Merrick Hale, washes into Coral's boathouse and trades a grease-stained map for a sworn promise: carry it to Ada Voss in Harrowgate before snowfall. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion hardening into obligation as Hale dies mid-sentence.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Navy investigators arrive asking about Hale; Coral lies badly and packs that night. His dive partner Juno insists on coming. Emotional beat: fear braided with the first flicker of loyalty — someone chose him, so he chooses back.

chapters.title: Harrowgate Road
chapters.summary: POV Juno. The pair reach the mining town of Harrowgate and find Ada Voss runs a roadhouse that serves everyone the law forgot. Emotional beat: wary hospitality — Ada reads the map, goes pale, and says only: 'You're eleven days late already.'

chapters.title: The Woman Who Kept the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Ada. She reveals her father was an engineer on the ship the navy sank — with witnesses aboard — and the map leads to the proof hidden in a high-valley cache. Emotional beat: grief converted to purpose; she agrees to guide them, over Coral's objection.

chapters.title: Syndicate Men at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Coral. A syndicate fixer named Corliss offers to buy the map, then threatens them when refused. A knife fight in the roadhouse kitchen leaves the place burning. Emotional beat: the point of no return — they flee into the foothills as wanted men.

chapters.title: Outcasts' Company
chapters.summary: POV Juno. On the trail they gather strays: Tam, a disgraced army tracker, and Wren, a teenage runaway who knows the high country. Emotional beat: friction becoming found family around a fire — jokes that mean more than they say.

chapters.title: The First Pass
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The company crosses Sawtooth Pass ahead of schedule but loses two mules and most of their food to a rockslide. Emotional beat: sobered resolve; Coral realizes the mountain is a third enemy counting down alongside navy and syndicate.

chapters.title: Corliss on Their Trail
chapters.summary: POV Tam. Tam spots syndicate riders paralleling them and lays a false trail through a burn scar. Emotional beat: quiet pride — the disgraced man proves his worth, and the group stops being strangers.

chapters.title: Wren's Shortcut
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Wren leads them through a canyon she alone knows, saving a day, but Coral nearly drowns in a flash flood — echoing his diver's life. Emotional beat: vulnerability; the team sees their leader can be saved, not just save.

chapters.title: The Cache Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They find her father's cache: a sealed strongbox of engineering logs proving the navy scuttled the ship to hide a failed weapons test, killing forty crew. Emotional beat: vindication and horror — the truth is heavier than any cargo.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Navy patrol intercepts them; an officer offers Coral amnesty and his old salvage license if he surrenders the logs. Coral refuses, and the patrol opens fire. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal — he chooses the dead crew over his own future.

chapters.title: Blood on the Scree
chapters.summary: POV Tam. The running fight costs Tam a shoulder wound and forces them off the main route into unmapped country. Emotional beat: grim endurance; Tam hides how bad the wound is, and Wren notices.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Weather turns; the early snows have come ahead of forecast. Juno calculates they have four days to cross Kestrel Pass or winter in above the treeline. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into focus — time is now the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Betrayal
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Corliss catches them at a waystation, having bought off their hired packer, who stole the strongbox overnight. Emotional beat: betrayal's sting — but Wren tracked the thief by instinct, giving them one desperate chance.

chapters.title: Recovery in the Dark
chapters.summary: POV Wren. A night raid reclaims the strongbox from the packer's camp; Coral spares the man's life and learns Corliss has orders to kill every witness, including Ada. Emotional beat: mercy as strength, and stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Kestrel Pass
chapters.summary: POV Ada. The final ascent through worsening snow; Tam collapses from his wound and insists they leave him. Instead they rope together and carry him. Emotional beat: the found family's creed stated aloud — nobody gets left on this mountain.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Storm hits at the crest; visibility zero, Corliss's men closing. Coral uses his diver's discipline — count breaths, trust the line — to lead them through the whiteout along a fixed rope. Emotional beat: everything he learned underwater saves them above the clouds.

chapters.title: The Descent and the Stand
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Cornered at a cliffside narrows, the company makes its stand. Tam, feverish but steady, holds the pass while Coral and Corliss fight hand-to-hand on the ice. Emotional beat: climax — Corliss falls to his death; the survivors stumble down into the valley, alive and changed.

chapters.title: Deliverance
chapters.summary: POV Ada. They reach the rail town of Verity and deliver the logs to a federal judge Ada has spent years cultivating. Emotional beat: release — the promise kept, Hale's dying request honored, the dead crew given names again.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The scandal breaks; the navy offers Coral hush money and reinstatement. He declines publicly, letting Ada's testimony stand instead. Emotional beat: quiet triumph — justice done without selling the truth back to the men who buried it.

chapters.title: When the Passage Wakes
chapters.summary: POV Coral, epilogue. Spring: the passes open, and Coral's old salvage claim is gone, seized in the fallout. But Juno, Tam, Wren, and Ada are waiting with a new boat and a new contract — honest work, together. Emotional beat: warm resolution; the wilderness forgave nothing, but it gave him a family that forgets less than any fortune.
